laws.rule: Louisiana bans using any wireless device while driving on public roads unless the vehicle is lawfully stationary (R.S. 32:59, as cited by the Highway Safety Commission). Exceptions include reporting a crash, emergency or serious hazard, hands-free GPS navigation and calling 911 to report a crime. In school zones and highway construction zones police can stop a driver for this alone; elsewhere it is enforced only alongside another violation. Officers issued only written warnings before 1 January 2026.
laws.penalty_signal: US$250 in school or construction zones (a judge may reduce it to US$100 with community service) and US$100 elsewhere (reducible to US$50); doubled if there is a crash (about A$355, A$142 and A$71 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026)

laws.rule: It is illegal to drive or ride in a moving vehicle with an open container of alcohol, and the rule covers every occupant (R.S. 32:300).

Drivers may not wear headphones or earbuds covering both ears (R.S. 32:295.2). Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, in poor visibility and whenever the wipers are needed for rain or moisture (R.S. 32:301, 32:322).
laws.penalty_signal: Headphones: US$25 (about A$36) plus court costs

laws.rule: New Orleans parade routes have their own rules under Municipal Code section 34-33, enforced by NOPD at Mardi Gras. Nothing may be placed on the public neutral ground (the grassy median) or along the route more than four hours before a parade starts. The city lists ladders taller than 6 feet, enclosures, open flames of any kind, gas or diesel generators, upholstered furniture, portable toilets, scaffolding, confetti guns, mylar balloons and unattended coolers as banned items. The page read did not give penalties or glass and alcohol-container rules.

items.text: Possessing 14 g or less of marijuana carries a fine of not more than US$100 (about A$142 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026) on any conviction, enforced by summons rather than arrest. More than 14 g: up to US$500 and six months on a first conviction, rising for repeats. Patients in the state medical program and visiting qualifying patients are exempt (R.S. 40:966).
